request: Please write me a complete, detailed month-by-month plan for a backyard vegetable garden for one full year. For each of the twelve months give what to sow, what to transplant, what to harvest and the main care jobs, with a short reason for each.
answer:
Here's a month-by-month vegetable garden plan for a full year. This is written for a generic temperate Northern Hemisphere climate (roughly USDA zones 5-7) — shift timing earlier if you're in a warmer zone, later if colder.

**January** — Sow: nothing outdoors; start onions/leeks indoors under lights (long season crops need the head start). Transplant: none. Harvest: stored root crops (carrots, potatoes, beets) from the cellar; overwintered kale/leeks if mild. Care: order seeds early for best variety availability; check stored produce for rot; service tools.

**February** — Sow: start tomatoes, peppers, eggplant indoors (8-10 weeks before last frost, since they're slow to mature); sow early lettuce/spinach under cover. Transplant: none yet. Harvest: remaining stored roots. Care: test soil pH/nutrients so amendments can work in before planting; chit seed potatoes (sprout them) for a head start.

**March** — Sow: direct-sow peas, spinach, radishes outdoors as soil becomes workable (cool-season crops tolerate frost); start brassicas (broccoli, cabbage) indoors. Transplant: harden off and transplant onion sets outdoors. Harvest: late winter greens if overwintered. Care: prepare beds — dig in compost (feeds soil biology before the growing rush); install pea/bean supports now while beds are empty.

**April** — Sow: direct-sow carrots, beets, lettuce, radish, Swiss chard (soil has warmed enough for germination). Transplant: brassica seedlings outdoors under row cover (protects from early pests/cold). Harvest: asparagus spears if established; early radishes. Care: mulch to suppress spring weeds before they establish; watch for slugs on tender seedlings.
